summary.text: Pat Harrigan, a West Point graduate and former Army Special Forces officer who co-owns firearms-industry businesses, is the Republican U.S. Representative for North Carolina's 10th Congressional District and won re-election on November 3, 2026, according to unofficial results. He lost the 2022 race for the 14th District to Democrat Jeff Jackson, then won the open 10th District seat in 2024. According to his House website, he is focused on national security and accountability in government.

paragraphs.text: Pat Harrigan was born in San Diego, California, in 1987, and earned a degree in nuclear engineering from the United States Military Academy at West Point in 2009.

According to his House website, he was commissioned as an Infantry officer after West Point and served at Fort Wainwright, Alaska; he deployed to Afghanistan as a platoon leader, then volunteered for and earned the Green Beret and returned to Afghanistan with Army Special Forces.
He was awarded two Bronze Stars and served in the U.S. Army from 2009 to 2014.

Harrigan began a small firearms business at home with his wife, Rocky, in 2015 while still on active duty, per his Ballotpedia survey; he co-owns ZRODelta, UnBrandedAR, and US Optics, which he says now operate from a 120,000-square-foot facility employing more than 50 people.
He ran in 2022 for the 14th District, losing the general election to Democrat Jeff Jackson, 57.7 percent to 42.3 percent.

In 2024 he won the Republican primary for the open 10th District seat with 41.2 percent over Grey Mills Jr. (38.9 percent) and others, then the general election with 57.5 percent over Democrat Ralph Scott Jr. (38.2 percent), Libertarian Steven Feldman, and Constitution Party candidate Todd Helm; he took office January 3, 2025.

For the 2025-2026 Congress he serves on the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology (Energy Subcommittee; Investigations and Oversight Subcommittee) and the House Committee on Armed Services (Intelligence and Special Operations Subcommittee; Military Personnel Subcommittee; Readiness Subcommittee).
According to his House website, Harrigan has been married to Rocky since 2010, and they have two daughters, Reagan and McKinley.
He won the November 3, 2026 general election with 49.7% of the vote to Ashley Bell's 48.7% and Steven Feldman's 1.6%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
